scope.method: Static baseline review only; no source changes, builds, test execution, emulator/device use, publishing, or visual inspection. LibraryPreferences.kt does not exist at this baseline; its entire object was read in AdvancedScreens.kt.

findings.evidence: Proven by the data flow when the last indexed member of a named collection is deleted or explicitly forgotten: collection chips are built from every value returned by LibraryPreferences.collections(), independently of the current files. LibraryRepository.delete (183-197) and forgetMissing (200-208) remove the index record but never remove collection:<uri>. Consequently the deleted file's collection remains selectable indefinitely and always yields an empty list when it has no remaining members. There is no collection-management/delete action for removing that orphan association; LibraryStreamingTest manually clears it in cleanup, so that test does not catch this condition.
findings.recommendation: Build visible collection names from memberships of URIs in the current file list; clear the URI's collection preference after a successful explicit delete/forget. Preserve associations for indexed records whose provider is merely offline or whose access was revoked.

findings.evidence: Conditional proven UI/action inconsistency: after availability becomes MISSING for a deleted local MediaStore row, previewAction blocks preview and the dedicated forget action appears, but Rename/Delete remain enabled and dispatch unchanged. AppRoot invokes LibraryRepository.rename/delete for them. For this proven-missing MediaStore URI, update/delete return 0 and their check fails, yielding generic error_storage instead of the known missing-file state. The same menu also dispatches external/share without the availability mapping. FileAccessUiTest only checks the row click and forget action; it does not check these menu actions.
findings.recommendation: For a confirmed MISSING record, disable or replace file-dependent rename/delete/external/share actions and retain details, collection metadata, history removal, and the explicit forget command. Route denied/unavailable states to their specific feedback where appropriate; do not classify them as missing.

findings.evidence: Proven under a nonempty library with blank search and a category, 100 MiB, or collection filter excluding all rows: filtered.isEmpty() shows no_files plus files_empty_body, which tells the user to start from Home to add a file. This is the same message as a genuinely empty library, although existing files become visible by clearing the filters. Only query text controls the alternative no_search_results message.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish an empty source library from an empty filtered result, and provide a clear-filters action or a filter-specific message for the latter.

test_gaps: No read test covers combined category/search/size/collection filters, ascending/descending sorting, or retention of those controls through refresh and collection editing.
Add a collection lifecycle regression: assign the sole file to a group, delete/forget it, and verify the group disappears; separately verify provider unavailability preserves the indexed membership.

Add menu-state tests for AVAILABLE, MISSING, PERMISSION_REQUIRED, UNAVAILABLE, and initial inspection-pending states. Existing FileAccessUiTest asserts only missing badge, row click, and forget dispatch.

Queue persistence/priority/pause/reordering have repository tests, but DownloadsScreen tab counts, search results/empty states, queue-only-paused start-button behavior, and displayed order versus priority execution are not covered by the read UI tests. Treat potential usability changes here as proposals, not additional proven failures.

DisplayFormatTest covers binary units, maximum Long and selected locales; add negative byte input and percent bounds/non-finite values if those inputs are part of the intended public contract. No proven formatting defect was found in the requested scope.
No tests were executed and no visual behavior was verified during this review.
